fields.sample_size: spatial analysis of informal settlements in the urban-forest interface zone (ZIUF) of Valparaiso, Chile, combining drone (RPAS) orthophotogrammetry, census land-ownership data and water coverage figures from private companies; no respondent sample
fields.effect_estimate: The absence of potable-water, sewerage, dry-network and stormwater infrastructure in the ZIUF, where most informal settlements are located, produces unequal access to water that maintains and reinforces socio-spatial exclusion; the authors attribute the infrastructure gap in part to water privatisation under the Chilean neoliberal model since the 1980s and to the informal land tenure that blocks formal service connection. Spatial descriptive analysis; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: spatial case study (drone orthophotogrammetry, census land tenure, utility coverage data)
fields.section: Full text: Methodology (RPAS survey, census, company coverage data); Results (coverage by settlement); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methodology (RPAS survey, census, company coverage data); Results (coverage by settlement); Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a spatial analysis of water infrastructure gaps in informal settlements of Valparaiso's urban-forest interface zone, read in full text 2026-10-04. Missing networks produce unequal access reinforcing exclusion; privatisation and informal tenure are cited as causes. Descriptive spatial case study.
pdf_note: Bitacora Urbano Territorial 30(1):151-165 (2020), about 56,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction partly different: the abstract emphasises privatisation (neoliberal model) as well as informal tenure. Tenure-linked service exclusion is direct evidence for 'formal connection' barriers.
